description: Intrusion-detection events: data source 2. Several providers may be active at once; every event names the provider that reported it, and the kind keeps a watermark per file.

cadences.basis: Survey, data source 2, "Sustainable polling frequency": alerts are low-volume and the backend re-reads the file backwards from the end on every call, so polling more often costs without benefit.

page_size.basis: 500 is the figure the collectors carried as a constant before the page became a setting, and nothing more: a documented starting point, not a measurement and not a survey figure. What an installation needs depends on how fast its sources write, which only that installation can measure: the collection surface measures it and suggests a pair. The default is within what the firewall serves for this read, so a database with no row never asks for a page the firewall would cut short.

sizing.basis: The alert query's `rowCount` defaults to 9999: a page this size is far beyond what an alert feed produces per poll.

bounds.name: rule_info_per_pass
bounds.basis: opnview's own, not a survey figure. Suricata's rule metadata is read one sid per request (survey, data source 2, "Rule metadata, read from source for step 6"), and each request runs a configd script on the firewall that opens the rule cache, so the bound caps the extra requests one 60-second alert pass makes. 25 a pass resolves 1 500 distinct rules an hour, beyond what any of the rulesets the survey met fires in a day; what is not asked carries over to the next pass that stores an event.

bounds.name: rule_info_recheck_seconds
bounds.basis: opnview's own, not a survey figure. A rule's metadata changes only when its ruleset is downloaded again, which OPNsense does on the schedule the user sets on Services > Intrusion Detection > Administration, commonly once a day; asking again after a day follows such a change within one update while costing at most one request per rule per day. It applies to found and not-found answers alike, so a rule installed after it was first asked about is found the next day.

functions.description: Called at every probe round: asks the firewall whether this implementation can be read and whether its configuration serves clients.
functions.name: probe

functions.description: Called before every read: which of the feed's files still exist, so a lost file is recorded as a permanent gap.
functions.name: rotation

functions.description: Called at every security-event pass: the newest page_size events, newest first.
functions.name: alerts

functions.description: Called after an alerts pass that stored at least one event, with the rule identities the provider's events carry that the rule-info cache holds no answer for, or an answer older than rule_info_recheck_seconds -- at most rule_info_per_pass of them. Its answers fill the cache; a call that fails fails nothing else, and the identities it did not answer are asked again.
functions.name: rule_info
